stem: What is the preferred modern management of a lateral cervical lymphatic malformation (cystic hygroma) to minimise morbidity?

options.text: Formal surgical excision with wide margins
Image-guided sclerotherapy using bleomycin or OK-432
Observation for spontaneous resolution at puberty
A prolonged course of broad-spectrum oral antibiotics

explanation: Image-guided sclerotherapy is the preferred modern management because it causes the lymphatic malformation to shrink while avoiding the morbidity of open surgery.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because wide surgical excision carries greater risk of morbidity, including injury to adjacent nerves and vessels.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because image-guided sclerotherapy with agents such as bleomycin or OK-432 induces fibrosis and shrinkage of the lymphatic malformation with less morbidity than surgery.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because these lesions do not usually resolve spontaneously, and symptomatic or enlarging malformations generally need active treatment.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because antibiotics may treat superimposed infection but do not treat the underlying lymphatic malformation.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because aspiration alone is temporary and does not provide definitive treatment for the malformation.

source.hint: Think about the interventional radiology techniques mentioned as being less invasive than surgery.
